rows.title: Discovery smoke tests + PRD/scope completion
rows.description: Arcane now has a plan to work inside OpenAI Codex, and a way to stop it flooding VS Code with duplicate spells when several Arcane projects are open at once — the plan, not the feature itself yet.

rows.title: Codex shim, repo tier (ships Codex)
rows.description: Codex can now see and run every Arcane spell — the first of three clients this program brings to parity.

rows.title: ADR ARC-045
rows.description: The architectural decision behind bringing every AI client to parity and fixing duplicate spells across projects is written down and accepted.

rows.title: Canonical move: `.arcane/spells/` + all clients as shims
rows.description: Every spell now has exactly one home, and Copilot, Claude Code and Codex all read from it through tiny generated pointers — spells can no longer drift between clients, and updating never silently overwrites a spell you customized.

rows.title: User tier install
rows.description: Install Arcane's spells once on your machine and every AI client — Codex, Copilot, Claude Code — finds them from any project, with nothing to configure and nothing of yours ever overwritten.

rows.title: Repo opt-out (`spell_scope`)
rows.description: Open several Arcane projects at once and you now see one set of spells instead of one set per folder — a repository can take its spells from your machine-wide install, and anything you edited is named rather than removed.

rows.title: Agents at the user tier
rows.description: Your Arcanos can now live once on your machine instead of once per project, and a project that takes its spells from there stops carrying its own copies of them.

rows.title: Distribution-model spike (restore-based delivery)
rows.description: Arcane looked hard at making spell files vanish from your repository and reappear on install, built the experiment, and decided against it: the user tier already removes the duplication, and a file git cannot see cannot carry your edits.
